title: Latency targets & acceptance criteria
description: The single source for the app's per-turn latency numbers, and the source the code reads. Loaded by the overlay's latency readout (frontend/decode.py -> Overlay.qml) and the orchestrator's latency table, so the numbers live in ONE place instead of the four they had drifted across. Each target has a 'ms' value, a 'kind', and a 'clock' describing exactly what is measured. Clock zero for the response metrics is 'end of speech' = the moment VAD DECLARES the turn over; the 1 s silence timer runs before that and is a turn-taking cost, not part of any budget here.
$comment: kind: 'floor' = a sub-second responsiveness acknowledgement (did it hear me / did it stop) — pass/fail, and a real product requirement independent of the screen. 'gate' = a pass/fail feedback guarantee. 'measured' = recorded per turn as a diagnostic and shown neutrally, NEVER pass/fail — the overlay must not flag it as over-budget. first_word is 'measured' because under generate-then-play first-word latency scales with reply length (~45 ms/token measured), so it is a reply-length proxy rather than a latency the system can tighten; and the streaming text on the island, not the first spoken word, is the first feedback anyway.

feedback.clock: end of speech -> first PERCEPTIBLE feedback: the overlay's state change to THINKING, the 'working' earcon, or the first spoken word — whichever lands first. The screen is the primary surface, so on a normal turn this is the near-instant flip to THINKING; the 'working' earcon (fired just before the deadline) is the speech-mode audio fallback.

first_word.clock: end of speech -> first spoken word (B1). Recorded, never pass/fail.

first_word_b2.clock: end of speech -> first spoken word (B2, local). Recorded, never pass/fail.

tool_ack.clock: end of speech -> Tier-2 starter-tool action executed (unbuilt)
